title: Affine quotients of smooth connected groups by multiplicative normal subgroups
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams; a homomorphism respects them. A group of multiplicative type of finite presentation is an fppf-local form of $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_S[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ as comultiplication [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Fppf means faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation with connected geometric fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $N\hookrightarrow H$ be a closed normal subgroup of multiplicative type of finite presentation [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then the fppf sheafification $J$ of $U\mapsto H(U)/N(U)$ is represented by a smooth affine $S$-group of finite presentation with connected geometric fibres. The map $q:H\to J$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented with scheme-theoretic kernel $N$, and $(h,n)\mapsto(h,hn)$ is an isomorphism $H\times_SN\simeq H\times_JH$. These assertions, including the identification as the fppf quotient, commute with arbitrary base change on $S$. No reductivity of $H$ and no smoothness of $N$ are required.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, quotient discussion, printed pp.97--98; smoothness and connected fibres by the fppf quotient. This is the smooth connected affine quotient prerequisite, without centre or maximal-torus conclusions. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Choose an fppf covering by affine schemes $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ on which $N_i\simeq D_{R_i}(M_i)$ with $M_i$ finitely generated; such a cover is precisely the multiplicative-type hypothesis, refined by affine open covers. The base changes $H_i$ are affine by affine-morphism permanence. Work on one such chart, writing $R,M,H,N$ and $A=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$. Right translation by $N$ gives the coaction $\rho:A\to A\otimes_RR[M]$. The action identities give its counit and coassociativity identities, so the coaction-grading lemma gives $A=\bigoplus_{m\in M}A_m$ with $\rho(b_m)=b_m\otimes e_m$. Put $B=A_0$.

source.place: Tag 0EKK (lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm): coefficient grading; arbitrary M supplied by the cited existing node.

proof.text:
The morphism $c:H\times_SN\to H\times_SH$, $(h,n)\mapsto(h,hn)$, is a closed immersion. Indeed, under the automorphism $(h,h')\mapsto(h,h^{-1}h')$, with inverse $(h,n)\mapsto(h,hn)$, it is the base change of the given closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow H$. Thus its map of affine coordinate rings is surjective. Under the affine tensor-product description that map is
$$\gamma:A\otimes_RA\longrightarrow A\otimes_RR[M],\qquad a\otimes b_m\longmapsto ab_m\otimes e_m.$$
For each $m$, lift $1\otimes e_m$ to a finite sum $\sum_k a_k\otimes b_k$. Expanding $b_k$ homogeneously and comparing the coefficient of $e_m$ gives $1=\sum_k a_k(b_k)_m$. Taking degree zero in $A$ gives $1=\sum_k(a_k)_{-m}(b_k)_m$. These are the homogeneous unit expressions required by the strong-grading lemma; no smoothness or centrality has entered.

source.place: Tag 0EKK coefficient extraction, combined with the closed subgroup and group identities; agent argument.

proof.text: Apply the strong-grading algebra theorem to get $Q_i=\operatorname{Spec}B\ $ and $q_i:H_i\to Q_i$, faithfully flat and finitely presented, together with $H_i\times_{S_i}N_i\simeq H_i\times_{Q_i}H_i$ whose projections are $h$ and $hn$. The quotient-sheaf identification is explicit. For a test scheme $T\to Q_i$, the base change $T\times_{Q_i}H_i\to T$ is an fppf cover and provides a lift to $H_i$. Two lifts have equal images exactly when their pair lies in the displayed fibre product, hence exactly when they differ by a unique section of $N_i$. Representable presheaves are fppf sheaves, by fpqc representable descent and the fppf-to-fpqc covering lemma. Therefore, for any fppf sheaf $F$, an orbit-presheaf map to $F$ extends uniquely to $h_{Q_i}$ by applying it to these local lifts and gluing; equality on overlaps and independence of lifts are the torsor identity. This proves the full sheafification universal property, also after any base change of $S_i$, because fppf covers base change and the torsor identity does too.

source.place: Tag 03C5 (lemma-criterion-quotient-representable), proof with the kernel pair; the sheafification argument is written out.

proof.text: Let $J$ initially denote the fppf sheafification in the statement. Its restriction to schemes over $S_i$ is the sheafification of the same orbit presheaf: coverings of such a test scheme and their refinements are identical in the big site and the slice site. Step 3 therefore identifies this restriction with $h_{Q_i}$. On overlaps these identifications induce unique scheme isomorphisms by Yoneda, satisfying the cocycle condition since their sheaf maps do. The locally representable-sheaf/descent-data theorem reduces representability of $J$ to effectiveness of this datum. Apply the fppf-family effectiveness criterion with the property 'affine morphism': affine permanence gives base-change stability and finite coproduct stability including the empty coproduct; its affine singleton hypothesis is precisely the existing effective fpqc descent theorem for affine morphisms, since an affine faithfully flat finitely presented cover is fpqc. Thus the datum is effective and $J$ is a scheme. Its map to $S$ is affine by fpqc descent of affineness, since each $Q_i\to S_i$ is affine and an fppf cover is fpqc. The quotient maps glue to $q:H\to J$ by their identical maps of sheaves and Yoneda.

The family $J_i=J\times_SS_i\to J$ is fppf by base change. The pullbacks of $q$ are the maps $q_i$ of step 3, so fpqc descent makes $q$ flat and locally of finite presentation. It is surjective: any point of $J$ lifts to a point of some $J_i$, and then lifts through the surjective $q_i$. The same descent of affineness applies to $q$, since the $q_i$ are affine by the strong-grading theorem. Thus $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by affine permanence, and therefore finitely presented. The canonical map $c:H\times_SN\to H\times_JH$ is an isomorphism: its pullback to every $S_i$ is the isomorphism in step 3; the local inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same map and glue by representable fpqc descent. The projection formulas are exactly $(h,n)\mapsto h,hn$.

Normality supplies the group structure without any additional representability input. For sections of $J$ choose fppf-local lifts $h,k$ in $H$ and define their product as $q(hk)$. Replacing lifts by $hn_1,kn_2$ changes the product to $hk(k^{-1}n_1k)n_2$, the same coset since $N$ is normal. Inverses and identity are similarly well defined, and sheaf gluing makes them global natural transformations. Yoneda turns them into scheme morphisms; the group diagrams and the homomorphism diagrams for $q$ hold after lifting, hence hold as sheaf identities. The kernel is exactly $N$: a section of $H$ maps to the identity if and only if it is fppf-locally in $N$, by the orbit-sheaf description; those local factorizations uniquely glue to a section of the representable sheaf $N$. This proves equality of the kernel functor and $h_N$, and Yoneda gives the scheme-theoretic cartesian kernel square.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); agent group-law argument on local coset representatives.

proof.text: Apply smooth source descent to $H\xrightarrow qJ\to S$: $q$ is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation by step 5, and the composite $H\to S$ is smooth by hypothesis. Hence $J\to S$ is smooth, in particular locally of finite presentation. Because it is affine it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so it is of finite presentation. For any geometric point $\bar s\to S$, $q_{\bar s}:H_{\bar s}\to J_{\bar s}$ is surjective (the singleton fppf cover base changes). Its source is connected and nonempty; the identity section also proves the target nonempty. If its target had a partition into two nonempty open-and-closed subsets, their inverse images would give such a partition of its source, contradicting connectedness. Therefore all geometric fibres of $J$ are connected.

source.place: Tag 05B5 (lemma-smooth-permanence); connectedness is the explicit inverse-image argument.

proof.text: Finally let $S'\to S$ be arbitrary. The singleton fppf covering $q$ base changes to an fppf covering $q':H_{S'}\to J_{S'}$; its kernel-pair isomorphism base changes with exactly the same two projection formulas. Repeating the local-lift and sheaf-gluing argument of step 3 proves directly that $J_{S'}$ sheafifies $H_{S'}(T)/N_{S'}(T)$, with no flatness assumption on $S'\to S$. The canonical comparison is the unique isomorphism commuting with the quotient maps. The descended group law is carried to the base-changed one because both send local lifted pairs to $q'(hk)$; the kernel is the base-changed kernel square. Smoothness base changes: $J\to S$ is smooth by step 7, i.e. affine-locally given by smooth ring maps $R\to C$ (the affine-local form recorded in the definition of smooth morphisms); $J_{S'}$ is covered by the affines $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_RC)$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq S'$ mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $R'\to R'\otimes_RC$ is smooth by base change of smooth ring maps. A geometric fibre of $J_{S'}$ over $\bar s'\to S'$ is the geometric fibre of $J$ over the composite $\bar s'\to S$, hence connected by step 7. Affineness and finite presentation base change by their cited permanence results. Thus every clause commutes with arbitrary base change; the proof never assumes reductivity of $H$ or smoothness of $N$.
